Documentation → Administration → Node TLS

Node TLS — the SATOM HTTPS certificate

Replace, issue and renew the HTTPS certificate the SATOM node itself serves, and watch each activation step — validate, write, nginx -t, reload, verify — as a job.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Certificates & Trust → Node TLS (URL /settings/#tab-nodetls)

What is it?#

Node TLS is the certificate the SATOM node presents to your browser and to its HA peer. nginx serves it on :443 (web access) and :8443 (node-to-node health probes) from the same configuration. On this tab you import a certificate from your own CA (pasted or uploaded), generate a CSR for an external CA, or issue one from SATOM's internal CA — and every activation runs as a job whose steps you watch live.

❗Important — The HA peer must trust this certificate

In a high-availability pair, each node verifies the other's :8443 certificate against its system trust store or the internal CA. A certificate that chains to neither (for example a self-signed one) is refused: the peer views stop showing data and the log names the reason. Use a CA-issued certificate, or one issued by the internal CA. See Security model.

ℹ️Note — Not the appliance certificates

Certificates on your appliances are managed in the Certificate Manager. The CAs SATOM trusts when it connects to an appliance are in the trust store.

What does it do?#

  • Shows the Service certificate (nginx :443 / :8443): subject, issuer, source and expiry.
  • Import certificate (PEM) — paste or upload certificate, private key and optional chain; validates the pair, installs it and rolls back automatically if nginx rejects it.
  • Certificate signing request (CSR) — generates a private key and CSR on the node; the key never leaves it. The certificate your CA returns is imported with the key field left empty.
  • Issue from internal CA — mints a certificate for the node host name from the internal CA, when this node holds the CA key.
  • Renew now — re-issues an internally issued certificate immediately (offered only when the served certificate was issued by the internal CA).
  • Renewal of an imported certificate — choose whether an imported certificate only raises an alert before expiry or is fetched again automatically over SSH, and test the pull with Test now.
  • Runs every activation as a job with visible steps, and warns you before nginx reloads.
  • Node-to-node encryption (Postgres replication) — shows the replication TLS state and lets you set the minimum TLS protocol and cipher list.

Requirements#

  • A host (non-container) installation for CSR generation and internal-CA issuance. In the container runtime, activation is delegated to the operations agent and only import is available.
  • Issue from internal CA needs the internal CA certificate and key on this node. Otherwise the button is disabled with the tooltip No internal CA key on this node (standby) — import instead.
  • For import: an unencrypted PEM private key that matches the certificate, or a certificate issued from a CSR generated on this node.

Permissions#

All Node TLS actions require users.manage (Administrator). The Certificates & Trust group of Settings is only offered to administrators; the underlying /settings/node-cert/… endpoints answer 403 to anyone else. See Permissions.

How to use#

Check the current certificate#

Open Settings → Certificates & Trust → Node TLS. The service certificate card shows Subject, Issuer, Source and Expires (with days left: red under 14 days, amber under 45). The source badge is one of:

Badge Meaning
CA-issued · auto-renew Issued by the internal CA; renewed automatically
imported Imported by an operator; SATOM alerts before expiry, or pulls the renewed files when Automatic pull is set (see below)
bootstrap (replace) The certificate created at installation; replace it

Import a certificate#

  1. In Import certificate (PEM), choose Paste PEM or Upload files. Only the visible mode is sent.
  2. Provide Certificate (PEM), Private key (PEM, unencrypted) and, if needed, Chain / intermediates (optional). Leave the key empty for a certificate issued from a CSR generated here.
  3. Click Validate & install and confirm the reload warning (see below).
  4. Follow the activation panel until it says done.

Get a certificate from an external CA (CSR)#

  1. In Certificate signing request (CSR), check Common name (pre-filled with this node's host name) and add Additional names (SAN) — host names or IP addresses, comma- or line-separated. The common name is always included.
  2. Optionally fill Organization, Organizational unit, City, State, Country (two letters) and choose the Key.
  3. Click Generate CSR. It appears under Pending CSRs (waiting for their certificate) with Copy, Download and Discard.
  4. Send the CSR to your CA. When the certificate comes back, import it with the private key empty — SATOM pairs it with the pending key.

Issue or renew from the internal CA#

  • Issue from internal CA mints a new certificate for the node host name and installs it (source becomes issued).
  • Renew now forces a re-issue of an issued certificate regardless of its expiry. For an imported or bootstrap certificate the button is disabled, with the tooltip Only a certificate issued by the internal CA can be renewed here — re-import, or use Automatic pull below.

The note under the service certificate card summarises the HA behaviour: CA-issued certificates are node-local (each HA node serves its own host name) and auto-renew nightly; an imported certificate is shared — the nightly pass publishes it from the node that serves it and installs it on the peer.

Renew an imported certificate automatically#

  1. In Renewal of an imported certificate, set When an imported certificate nears expiry to Alert only (default) or Automatic pull (fetch the renewed files over SSH and install them).
  2. For automatic pull, fill Source host, SSH port, SSH user, Authentication (Key file on this node with Key file path, or Password — blank keeps the stored one), Remote certificate path, Remote private key path and optionally Remote chain path (optional).
  3. Click Save renewal settings. The line under the form reads Saved — mode: … or the reason for a refusal.
  4. Click Test now and confirm Run one automatic pull now? If the source holds a newer certificate it is installed and nginx is reloaded on this node. The pull runs once whatever the mode: it fetches the files, checks that the key matches, and installs them only when they are newer than the served certificate. The result reads Pulled and installed. or the reason (for example that the certificate is up to date).

Watch the activation#

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Renew now is offered only for a certificate issued by the internal CA, and the new Renewal of an imported certificate card sets the renewal mode and runs Test now; the page also states that an imported certificate is shared between HA nodes.

Every Validate & install, Issue from internal CA and Renew now first asks for confirmation with this text:

This reloads nginx on this node to switch to the new certificate.

Open connections — this page included — move to the new certificate. If the page stops responding or the browser shows a certificate warning, close every browser window and open SATOM again.

Continue?

While the job runs, the Activating certificate panel shows the warning nginx is reloaded on this node to switch to the new certificate. Your session is kept, but open connections — this page included — move to the new certificate. If the page stops responding or the browser shows a certificate warning, close every browser window and open SATOM again: the browser keeps the certificate it had already accepted for this address.

The steps appear one by one, each with running / ok / warning / failed state:

  1. 1ValidateValidate the certificate, key and chain (import) — or Mint a certificate from the internal CA (issue / renew)
  2. 2WriteWrite the certificate and key (previous pair kept for rollback)
  3. 3nginx -tTest the nginx configuration (nginx -t)
  4. 4ReloadReload nginx
  5. 5VerifyCheck that nginx serves the new certificate

If a step fails, Restore the previous certificate runs and the panel says The previous certificate was put back; nginx keeps serving it. After a successful reload the panel shows nginx was reloaded with the new certificate. If this or another SATOM tab stops responding or shows a certificate warning, close every browser window and open SATOM again. and a Reload this page button.

If the browser briefly loses the connection, the panel shows No answer from this node — expected for a moment while nginx switches certificate. Still checking… and keeps polling for up to three minutes; the outcome is always kept on the Jobs page.

Tune replication TLS#

In Node-to-node encryption (Postgres replication), pick the Minimum TLS protocol (TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3), optionally a Cipher list (OpenSSL syntax), and click Apply protocol & ciphers. It applies to this node's PostgreSQL and reloads it. Encryption enforcement itself is set at installation.

Configuration#

Import

Field Description Required Example
Certificate (PEM) The leaf certificate; file types .pem, .crt, .cer Yes -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----…
Private key (PEM, unencrypted) Must match the certificate; leave empty for a CSR generated here Yes, unless from a local CSR -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…
Chain / intermediates (optional) Appended after the leaf in the served file No intermediate CA PEM

Each slot takes a file or pasted text, never both.

CSR

Field Description Required Example
Common name Host name or IP; defaults to the node host name Yes (pre-filled) satom.example.com
Additional names (SAN) Extra host names / IPs No satom-2.example.com, 192.0.2.10
Organization / Organizational unit / City / State Optional subject attributes (64 characters max each) No Example Corp
Country Two-letter ISO code No CH
Key RSA 2048, RSA 3072, RSA 4096, ECDSA P-256, ECDSA P-384 Yes RSA 2048

Example#

🧪Example — Replace the bootstrap certificate with one from the company CA

  1. Node TLS shows source bootstrap (replace).
  2. Generate CSR with common name satom.example.com, SAN satom.example.com, key RSA 2048. Download the CSR and submit it to the company CA.
  3. Paste the returned certificate into Certificate (PEM), the CA's intermediate into Chain / intermediates (optional), leave the key empty, Validate & install, confirm.
  4. The panel shows Validate the certificate, key and chain with · key from the pending CSR, then write, nginx -t, reload and nginx presents the new certificate on :8443. Source is now imported.
  5. Close and reopen the browser if it still shows the old certificate.

Result#

  • The new certificate and key are written for nginx (key mode 0600); the previous pair is kept for rollback. The source (imported or issued) is recorded.
  • A job node_cert_import, node_cert_issue or node_cert_renew with its steps, visible under Jobs.
  • Audit log entries: node_cert.import, node_cert.issue, node_cert.renew (or …_failed), node_cert.csr, node_cert.csr_discard, node_cert.renew_mode, node_cert.autopull, pg_ssl.policy.
  • A row in the renewal journal, shown on Certificate Manager → Renewals.
  • A pending CSR is deleted once its certificate is installed; at most the 10 newest pending CSRs are kept.

Troubleshooting#

"private key does not match the certificate"#

Possible causes — the key belongs to another certificate (for example an earlier CSR).

Solution — import the matching key, or leave the key empty if the certificate came from a CSR generated on this node.

Verification — the Validate the certificate, key and chain step turns green.

"private key is not valid PEM (or is passphrase-protected): …"#

Remove the passphrase from the key (or export it unencrypted) and import again.

"no private key given, and no CSR generated on this node matches this certificate …"#

Possible causes — the key field was left empty, but the certificate was not issued from a pending CSR on this node (or that CSR was discarded or pruned, or was generated on the other HA node).

Solution — paste or upload the private key. A discarded CSR's key no longer exists anywhere; generate a new CSR and have it signed again.

"the certificate was given both as a file and as pasted text — keep one"#

The same slot was filled in both modes. Keep only one (the error names the slot: certificate, key or chain).

"nginx -t failed: …"#

Possible causes — nginx rejected its configuration with the new files.

Solution — nothing to undo: the previous certificate was restored. Read the nginx message in the step detail, fix the material and import again.

"sudo refused the nginx reload … and the root runner did not pick up the request within 90s. Check that the runner is armed: systemctl enable --now satom-updater.path"#

Possible causes — the host's sudo policy does not honour SATOM's allowlist, so the reload was handed to the root runner, which is not active.

Solution — on the node, run systemctl enable --now satom-updater.path, then repeat the activation. sudo -l -U satom (or the service account chosen at installation) shows what sudo allows.

"internal CA key not present on this node — import a certificate instead"#

This node holds no internal CA key (typically a standby joined without it). Import a certificate, or re-run the installer's node-join step with the cluster join key so the node receives the CA.

The job ends "done with a warning"#

Possible causes — the files are in place and nginx accepted them, but Check that nginx serves the new certificate still saw the previous certificate on :8443 (or could not connect) after 10 seconds.

Solution — reload the page after a few seconds; if the old certificate persists, check that the nginx site uses SATOM's certificate files.

The HA peer shows "unreachable" after a certificate change#

Possible causes — the new certificate does not verify on the other node (it chains to neither the system trust store nor the internal CA), so the peer refuses its requests instead of sending them unverified. The peer's log reads peer TLS refused for <host>: peer TLS certificate did not verify ….

Solution — install a certificate the other node trusts. SATOM_PEER_TLS_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 in .env restores an encrypted-but-unverified retry as a temporary emergency override only; remove it once the certificate is fixed.

Verification — on High Availability, the peer's Health is up again.

The browser still shows a certificate warning after a successful change#

The browser keeps the certificate it already accepted for this address. Close every browser window and open SATOM again.

Advanced#

Advanced Automatic renewal and expiry alerts
  • satom-cert-renew.timer runs daily at 03:30 (with up to 30 minutes of random delay). It re-issues an issued certificate within 30 days of expiry; imported and bootstrap certificates are skipped and recorded as such. Internally issued certificates are valid for 825 days.
  • The same nightly pass handles imported certificates according to the renew mode set in Renewal of an imported certificate (alert by default; autopull fetches the renewed pair over SSH from the configured source). The mode is also shown on the Renewals page.
  • The alert engine's certificate check (on by default) warns before the service certificate expires (threshold in Settings → Email & Alerts, default 14 days).
  • Certificate Manager → Renewals → Run renewal pass now, or satom execute cert renew on the node, runs the pass immediately. satom get certificate status and satom diagnose certificate report the served certificate and the last renewal result.
Advanced High availability

Each node serves its own certificate. In the nightly pass, an imported certificate is published to a shared slot under the data directory, which the HA data sync carries to the peer; the peer installs it only if it covers the peer's host name, through the same validate → nginx -t → rollback path. Internally issued and bootstrap certificates name one node and are never shared. Generated CSR keys stay on the node that created them.

Advanced How the reload is performed

nginx -t and systemctl reload nginx are run through a sudo allowlist. If sudo refuses (password required, user not allowed, no sudo), the same test and reload are handed to the root runner and the job waits up to 90 seconds for its verdict. A genuine nginx -t failure is reported, never retried.
